body:
There is an error that prevents your `total_cost` relation from working.

Notice that `subT` starts with a lowercase letter. This makes it a constant atom rather than a variable. You're essentially saying that for a list `[H | T]`, the `total_cost` of its tail `T` must be the constant `subT`.

Once `total_cost` reaches the base case, unification fails immediately, because `total_cost([], subT).` does not exist—0 is not equal to the literal atom `subT`, so for any given array other than the empty array, your `total_cost` will fail.

This is easy to fix, luckily! You just need to make sure `SubT` is capitalized so that it's a variable instead of a constant. By doing so, when you reach the base case with total 0, your variable is able to bind to the value, so you can successfully bind each subtotal to the sum of the integer `H` and the previous subtotal.
